clue.text: With Ucas service, that person's receiving answer relieving tension

indicators.note: a word that is receiving something takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Clearing is the UCAS process matching unplaced applicants to spare university places

explanation.surface: A university admissions helpline with a sympathetic voice on the end soothes an anxious applicant.
explanation.walkthrough: UCAS is the UK body that handles university applications; its Clearing stage matches late applicants to spare places. 'That person's' uses singular they.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing the air is an idiom for easing a strained atmosphere by talking a problem through.

clue.text: Respite oldest puppy regularly required

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is taken

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone with an elderly dog says the old thing needs a break now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing off, the same as a respite from effort or trouble.

clue.text: One broadcasting first of snooker frames

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A television station showing the snooker gets the first frames on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frames' looks like part of a snooker match, but it is the definition: clothes-drying racks.
explanation.definitionFit: Airers are folding racks on which washing is hung to dry, so they are frames.

clue.text: This writer's shames penning extremely unpopular dirty content

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the outer word holds another inside
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

blocks.note: the setter says I'm, I am
a shame is a pity, plural here

explanation.surface: A writer confesses embarrassment at having produced unpopular smutty material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shames' is a plural noun, as in 'what a shame', not the verb it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Impurities are contaminating substances, the dirty matter contained in something otherwise clean.

clue.text: People admired one providing unexpected help, no end

indicators.note: no end tells us the word end itself is taken away from the longer word

blocks.note: a godsend is a welcome stroke of luck
the word itself, to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone who helped out of the blue becomes endlessly admired.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'end' is not the last letter but the three letters END themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolised celebrities are called gods, as in footballing gods, people worshipped by fans.

clue.text: Restrain brash journo, so Spooner says

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: bold is brash and a hack is a journalist; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: An editor tells an overconfident reporter to rein it in, in Spooner's muddled words.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back is to check or restrain someone or something from acting.

clue.text: Bug coming from silver grille outside V&A

indicators.note: outside means one word goes round the other, surrounding it

blocks.note: a grate is a metal grille

explanation.surface: A silver grille installed outside the Victoria and Albert Museum causes irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; its initials sit inside GRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, and aggravate in informal use means annoy or irritate.

clue.text: Be like kinsfolk and jog during race

blocks.note: to jog is to run gently
race in the sense of a line of descent, a lineage

explanation.surface: A family whose members all take part in a jog during a running race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a running event next to 'jog', but it means lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait that runs in the family is shared by relatives, so having it means resembling one's kin.

clue.text: Strong currents decreasing flow at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Ocean currents weakening their flow out on the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currents' suggests water, but here it means currents of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Gale-force winds are very powerful air movements, and air currents are winds.

clue.text: Method hard with surgery cutting into stick insect, say

indicators.note: cutting into means one piece slices its way inside another

blocks.note: an art is a technique or method

explanation.surface: A tricky surgical procedure performed on a stick insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick insect' looks like one creature, but 'stick' belongs to the wordplay and 'insect, say' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are one example of arthropods, invertebrates with jointed legs and an exoskeleton; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Name of man that's shelled egg in advance

indicators.note: shelled means with its shell removed, so the outer letters go and only the middle stays
in places one piece inside another

explanation.surface: A man known for having shelled an egg ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Logan is a common male first name, so it is a name a man might have.

clue.text: This leader Nap might be interpreted to give proper name

indicators.note: interpreting reads letters in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
the answer together with Nap gives the longer phrase, so Nap is taken out of it to leave the answer's letters

blocks.note: letters to take out of the pool

explanation.surface: Napoleon's nickname Nap needs interpreting to reveal the leader's proper name.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer plus NAP rearranges to PROPER NAME, so remove NAP from those letters and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon, often shortened to Nap, was Emperor of the French, so 'this leader' is an emperor.

clue.text: Get over this country losing final in soccer against Italy

indicators.note: losing means something is lost, so letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: the last letter of soccer set beside I, the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Britain gets beaten in a football match against Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' reads as a match fixture, but it only means 'next to', joining the two letters lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, which is one everyday sense of get.

clue.text: New organism to expert in cultivation

indicators.note: new suggests something made over, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newly bred organism is handed to a specialist grower.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist is a scientist of soil management and crop production, an expert in growing things.

clue.text: River banks abandoned by rodent hunter

indicators.note: the banks are the edges, and abandoning them removes the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cat that hunts rats along a river abandons the banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is an English river, so the word fits a plain definition by name.

clue.text: Puzzle about time cleric turned revolutionary

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the others
turned means flipped round, so the whole assembled string is read from the end

explanation.surface: A priest has been baffled, over time, after switching to radical politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like an adjective tied to 'turned', but it is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A subverter undermines an established system, like a revolutionary seeking to overthrow it.

clue.text: Transport guns about with every one bearing company abbreviation

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards
bearing means carrying, so one word holds the abbreviation inside it

blocks.note: gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A delivery of firearms where every crate bears the firm's abbreviated name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach is a horse-drawn coach carrying passengers along a regular route, a form of transport.

clue.text: Return note wrapped around returned gold particle

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from right to left
wrapped around means encasing, so the first pair goes round the second

blocks.note: to return a candidate is to elect them

explanation.surface: A returned note comes wrapped round a gold fleck that had been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' is a verb meaning vote in, not a reversal signal; the reversal is 'returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a subatomic particle carrying negative charge.

clue.text: Horsemen around globe backed by deity

explanation.surface: Riders travel round the world supported by a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballeros is Spanish for gentlemen riders; in English it means horsemen or cavaliers.

clue.text: Grumble losing heart in faith

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so losing it drops the middle letters

explanation.surface: A complaint from someone whose faith is wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: BELIEF has six letters, so its heart is the central pair LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a complaint or grievance, so it means a grumble.

clue.text: One seeing that toff climbing tree

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: as means since or seeing that
nob is slang for a posh person

explanation.surface: Someone watches a posh gent scramble up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree grown in a pot.

clue.text: One miserable with uncovered arm cut

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so only the inside letter is kept

blocks.note: to etch is to cut into a surface

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy after a cut on their bare arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unhappy, unfortunate person, so one who is miserable.

clue.text: Arboreal beast nicked some soup, naughtily

indicators.note: nicked means docked, so the word loses its tail
naughtily suggests misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in line

blocks.note: the word with its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A tree-dwelling animal mischievously stole some soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' reads as stole, but it cuts the end off the word some.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is an American marsupial that lives largely in trees, an arboreal animal.

clue.text: Hoofed beast traversing North Pole

indicators.note: traversing means passing across, so the outer word straddles the letter inside

explanation.surface: A deer crosses the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Pole' looks like one place, but 'Pole' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stang is a dialect word, chiefly Scots and northern English, for a pole or wooden bar.

clue.text: Join together following work

blocks.note: to use something is to work it

explanation.surface: Two parts are joined after some work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse is to unite or blend things into one, as metals are fused by heat.

clue.text: Refusal to move forward in voice recorder

indicators.note: moving forward shifts a chunk to the front of the word

blocks.note: the word of refusal found in the middle of the voice, which is the chunk that moves

explanation.surface: A singer's refusal to step forward is captured by a recording device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a machine or a flute, but here it is simply a person who notes things down.
explanation.definitionFit: A noter is someone who notes things down, a person who records.

clue.text: Delete lines on a French social media platform

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it, so this piece is sent to the end

explanation.surface: An instruction to delete some lines posted on a French social media site.
explanation.definitionFit: To uninstall software is to remove it from a device, deleting the program.

clue.text: TV series is one I've never seen, working nights

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over, so the letters are put to a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they have never watched a TV show because they work nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger Things is a Netflix science-fiction drama, so it is a television series.
